one_liner: A habit tracker that forgives missed days — streak repair and weekly targets instead of daily guilt.
description: Streakly is an iOS habit tracker built around a simple observation: people quit habit apps the day they break a streak. Streakly lets you repair a missed day by doubling up within the week, scores habits against weekly targets rather than unbroken daily chains, and keeps everything private on-device. No social feed, no leaderboards, no shame mechanics.
target_user: People who have abandoned two or three habit apps already

icp.who: Adults 25-45 who keep restarting habit systems every January and abandoning them by February
icp.pain: One missed day breaks the streak, the streak was the motivation, and the app gets deleted in the guilt spiral that follows
icp.buying_trigger: A fresh-start moment — new year, new job, post-vacation — combined with memory of the last abandoned tracker

differentiators: Streak repair: make up a missed day within the week and the chain survives
Weekly-target scoring designed around behavior-change research, not gamified guilt
Private by default — on-device data, no accounts, no social feed
proof_points: 41% of an 800-person TestFlight cohort still tracking at day 30
Most-requested feature (streak repair) shipped as the core mechanic, not an IAP
pricing_current: free during beta (premium tier planned at $29/year)

voice.sample_phrase: Missed a day? Repair it. Your streak survives real life.

signals: Weekly beta builds with release notes

gaps: No website beyond a one-page waitlist

confidence.notes: Mechanic and voice are well evidenced from the beta. Retention stats are self-reported from a single cohort.
